standard.title: Identify audience and purpose
standard.description: identify the audience and purpose of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts, and discuss how language features are used to engage and influence the intended audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify the purpose and audience of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts (AC9E2LY03). They have not yet discussed how specific language features engage or influence the intended audience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify the audience and purpose of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts and discuss how language features engage and influence the intended audience.

nodes.label: Identifying audience and purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify the intended audience and purpose of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the audience and purpose of at least two texts of different types (imaginative, informative or persuasive) and explain the evidence that shows each.
nodes.typical_width: Identify the audience and purpose of imaginative, informative and persuasive texts; identify words, phrases and images intended to persuade; identify the purpose of imaginative texts.
wider: Find a text where the intended audience is not explicit and discuss how you work out who it is from clues in the text
Compare two advertisements targeting different age groups and identify the specific features that signal each audience
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot reliably identify the intended audience and purpose of a text cannot proceed to N2 — explaining how language features engage or influence requires knowing which audience and what purpose they are serving.

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate examples across imaginative, informative and persuasive text types before the audience/purpose identification schema becomes reliable. A single text type is insufficient — the concept needs to crystallise across the full range before N2 analysis is workable.

success_criteria: Student identifies the intended audience and purpose of a text
Student provides at least one textual feature as evidence for their identification

nodes.label: Language features that engage and influence
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss how specific language features in texts engage the intended audience or work to persuade them.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one language feature in a persuasive or advertisement text and explain how it is designed to engage or persuade the target audience.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss how language features (including words, phrases and images) are used to engage and influence the intended audience across persuasive and imaginative texts — connecting feature choices to audience and purpose.
wider: Examine features of advertisements specifically targeting children and discuss how the language choices exploit what children find appealing or trustworthy
Compare how an imaginative text engages its audience differently from a persuasive text — identifying what different types of engagement look like

response_modes.reason: Connecting a language feature to its audience-influencing effect requires explicit reasoning — students need the chain: feature → how it works on this audience → the effect it creates. Without scaffolding, students say features are 'persuasive' without explaining why.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Advertisements targeting children are a rich and directly relevant context at Y3. Students can critically examine texts designed to influence them specifically — which is both educationally powerful and motivating at this age.
success_criteria: Student identifies a language feature and names the intended audience
Student explains how the feature is designed to engage or persuade that specific audience
